title: True Roman doctrine on images is drawn from general Councils, universal practice, and common doctor-consensus
source_text: II. Ut autem certo habeatur, quae sit vera doctrina Ecclesiae Romanae de cultu imaginum, primo consulenda sunt Concilia quae apud ipsam habentur pro generalibus, & a Pontifice Romano probatis. Praeterea videndum est quae sit Universalis & apud omnes recepta Ecclesiae istius praxis. Denique examinandum est quid ea de re statuat communis doctorum in ea receptorum consensus. Nam ex tribus hisce fontibus hauriri potest vera & genuina Ecclesiae Romanae doctrina. Ac tanquam fidei Romanae dogma tuto haberi potest quod est in Generalibus Ecclesiae Romanae Conciliis definitum, quod firmat ejus praxis Universalis, & quod communi consensu Doctores illius tenent & amplectuntur.
pass_a_gloss: But that it may be certainly had what is the true doctrine of the Roman Church concerning the cult of images, first the Councils are to be consulted which are held among her as general and approved by the Roman Pontiff. Besides, it is to be seen what is the Universal practice of that Church, received among all. Finally it is to be examined what the common consensus of the doctors received in her decides on that matter. For from these three sources the true and genuine doctrine of the Roman Church can be drawn. And that which is defined in the General Councils of the Roman Church, which her Universal practice confirms, and which the Doctors of that Church hold and embrace by common consensus, can safely be held as a dogma of the Roman faith.
pass_b_english: Three wells yield Rome’s real teaching on images: general Councils Rome owns, her universal practice, and the received doctors’ consensus.
What those three agree on may safely be called Roman dogma.

choices.why: Method thesis: sources that fix what Rome truly teaches.
